caveats: Needs two concurrent requests landing in the window: CheckoutComplete plus a checkout-modifying request (e.g. the same customer in a second tab/device adding lines or changing address) or a staff shipping-admin mutation.
Needs concurrently served requests (threads, processes or workers) with separate DB connections; deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.

Needs a DB where the validation-read/order-write interleaving is possible (Postgres read-committed, the default engine per saleor/settings.py:62); stricter isolation or a serialized test backend narrows the window.
Relies on payment-gateway network-call behaviour and Postgres read-committed semantics, both outside this tree.
subclaims.reason: CheckoutComplete.perform_mutation fetches the checkout with no row lock at saleor/graphql/checkout/mutations.py:693-708 and validates it once via clean_checkout at mutations.py:712, which calls is_valid_shipping_method at saleor/checkout/utils.py:797-801 querying the currently applicable methods. The same in-memory checkout.shipping_method is then copied into the order with no revalidation by _process_shipping_data_for_order at saleor/checkout/utils.py:567-571 inside prepare_order_data's separate transaction (mutations.py:716-736), persisted by Order.objects.create in create_order at saleor/checkout/utils.py:737, with the payment-gateway network call at mutations.py:747-753 sitting between validation and insert. Between the validation SELECTs and the order INSERT, a concurrent request can commit changes making the method inapplicable: the customer's own second request (CheckoutLinesAdd/Update/Delete at mutations.py:308/356/369 changing subtotal/weight, or CheckoutShippingAddressUpdate at mutations.py:471 changing country, the exact inputs applicability is computed from at saleor/shipping/models.py:99-133) or a staff request (ShippingZoneUpdate/Delete, ShippingPriceUpdate/Delete at saleor/graphql/shipping/mutations.py:145/162/268/294 changing zones/limits). The completing request never sees this because it reuses the already-fetched checkout.shipping_method object and runs no validity query after mutations.py:712, while nothing locks the checkout or shipping rows (the only locks in the flow cover vouchers and gift cards at saleor/checkout/utils.py:530/747). Under read-committed the other transaction's commit lands between the validation reads and the order write, so the order is created carrying a method the validation query would now reject, a TOCTOU the codebase itself acknowledges by re-checking the method after every line/address change at mutations.py:350/393/518. The window spans DB round-trips and an external payment call, all of which release the GIL, and concurrent requests may run in separate threads, processes or workers sharing no GIL, so the interleaving is reachable on CPython with the GIL.
